title: Coal India unit Mahanadi's IPO fully subscribed on final day, led by institutional investors - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Mahanadi Coalfields' initial public offering was fully subscribed on ​the third and final day of bidding on Monday, ‌with large institutional investors leading demand.

The company sought ​a valuation of $9.6 billion and is ⁠the third unit of state-owned Coal India, the world's biggest coal miner, to go public this year as the ‌government pursues a divestment programme. Mahanadi accounts for about a fifth of India's coal production.

The ‌IPO was entirely an offer-for-sale, with existing investors ‌diluting ⁠their stakes. Coal India planned to ⁠sell around 662 million shares, or a 10 per cent stake, and anchor investors bought a portion, leaving about 493 million for other ​investors.

The share sale received ‌bids for 736.3 million shares, as of 3:45 PM IST, exchange data showed.

Qualified institutional investors bid for nearly five times their portion, while non-institutional ‌and retail investors subscribed 0.65 times and 0.43 ​times their portion.

Chola Securities said Mahanadi's strong market position, infrastructure, reserves and balance sheet ⁠support resilience, but weak revenue growth, margin pressure and the energy transition could weigh on its long-term ‌growth and profitability.

Coal India is expected to raise about $963 million at the upper end of a price band of ₹129 to ₹136 each.

Last week, Mahanadi Coalfields said it would raise ₹2,295 crore ($247.08 million) from anchor investors, including Abu Dhabi ‌Investment Authority and Life Insurance Corporation of India.

As India seeks ​to raise domestic coal production and limit imports, Mahanadi serves as a critical coal ⁠supplier to the country's power plants.

Two of Coal India's ⁠other subsidiaries, Bharat Coking Coal and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute , were listed earlier this ‌year. Another unit, South Eastern Coalfields, filed its draft IPO papers earlier this month.
